one_line: A website-enforced authority layer that bounds consequential WebMCP agent actions.
what_it_does: Publishes page-defined tools while enforcing live delegated limits, exact approvals, and session-scoped authority for billing actions.
leverage_rationale: The core value is changing WebMCP from capability exposure into execution-time authority enforcement with shared live state; generic UI-driving agents would be less reliably constrained.
leverage_evidence: Description says the website, not the prompt, enforces authority at execution time.
Claimed blocked €1,200 refund under €500 cumulative limit, then live €800 session authority and approval-bound remainder.
Frame sheet visibly shows an authority/security product and Control Center, though exact flow is not legible.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent end-to-end safety workflow and has a live demo, public repository, and frame-sheet evidence, but no video or transcript and the screenshots do not prove every claimed state.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repository are reported alive.
Claimed workflow covers invoice inspection, contract verification, authority read, blocked attempt, replanning, approval, and final-state verification.
Frame sheet shows consistent product surfaces including overview, configuration, and Control Center.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete high-stakes problem for teams deploying browser agents against billing and sensitive business systems, with a credible safety mechanism.
impact_evidence: Billing dispute scenario uses refunds and account credits as consequential actions.
Description directly frames stale or manipulated prompts as inadequate guardrails.
Human approval and audit/state visibility are central to the demonstrated use case.
creativity_rationale: The capability-versus-authority framing and website-enforced, session-scoped governance are a strong synthesis for WebMCP, though the general authorization concept is established.
creativity_evidence: Core thesis explicitly separates what an agent can do from what it is authorized to do now.
Authority changes without restarting the agent, requiring rereading and replanning.
Exact-action approval binding is a thoughtful interaction model.
usability_note: The visible dark dashboard and structured controls look coherent, but small frame evidence cannot establish operational usability.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; central agent invocation is claimed rather than directly evidenced.
Many detailed claims in the packet are not independently observable from the supplied frame sheet.
standouts: Strong separation of capability and authority.
Live, session-scoped limit changes with blocked-action semantics.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-native safety concept with credible impact and a coherent claimed workflow, despite limited direct execution evidence.

one_line: An agent-led airline lost-property investigation with matching and owner verification.
what_it_does: Creates a claim, checks flight context, searches found inventory, compares similar candidates, and asks for private ownership evidence before recovery.
leverage_rationale: Structured search, matching, verification, and claim state make a natural-language investigation substantially more reliable than an agent manually navigating disparate airline forms and pages.
leverage_evidence: One request is claimed to create a claim, check flight data, search inventory, and compare candidates.
Demo intentionally includes wrong-flight, partial, and strong matches.
Private identifying detail is withheld from public listing and agent until the human supplies it.
execution_rationale: The scenario is unusually well specified and includes adversarial near-matches and an ownership gate; no public repository and no video lower confidence in completeness.
execution_evidence: Live demo reported alive with three frame sheets and Devpost screenshot.
Claimed investigation has multiple realistic candidate outcomes rather than a single perfect match.
Human ownership evidence is verified against a private record.
impact_rationale: Lost-property recovery is a clear, recurring travel pain point, and the product addresses uncertainty across airline and airport channels while preserving ownership control.
impact_evidence: Description identifies the practical confusion over airline versus airport reporting.
Agent handles claim creation, flight lookup, found-item search, and follow-up.
Ownership verification reduces the risk of falsely claiming a similar item.
creativity_rationale: The combination of agent investigation, intentionally ambiguous matching, and private owner-only evidence is a fresh and memorable application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Near-match inventory is designed to force investigation.
Owner-only red-keychain detail creates a meaningful human-agent interaction rather than automatic matching.
usability_note: The stated single-request workflow is approachable, though visual evidence was not sufficiently legible to assess polish.
red_flags: No public repository and no video/transcript.
End-to-end recovery completion is claimed but not directly demonstrated in readable evidence.
standouts: Private ownership evidence keeps matching from becoming an unsafe auto-claim.
advance_reason: Clear audience and strong WebMCP fit through structured investigation and human ownership verification.

one_line: A cooperative puzzle game where a human and an AI-controlled robot must coordinate.
what_it_does: The human moves one character while the agent reads boards, moves the robot, hints, resets, changes levels, and speaks; intentionally missing human-control tools force cooperation.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the game mechanic: structured tools give the agent only robot-side actions, while the human retains indispensable actions. A generic UI-driving agent would undermine the designed capability boundary.
leverage_evidence: Agent has six explicit tools but no tool to move the human character.
Solver verifies each level is solvable yet not solvable with the robot frozen.
Three levels require the human and robot to coordinate through tool calls and conversation.
execution_rationale: The packet provides unusually concrete implementation and validation details for a compact scope, including a joint-state solver and deliberate level constraints; no frames were submitted.
execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo are reported alive.
Vanilla JavaScript static implementation with level data, movement rules, renderer, and BFS solver.
Claimed solver-based prevalidation rejects levels solvable single-handed.
impact_rationale: It offers a clear, accessible demonstration of human-agent teamwork and can teach the value of capability boundaries, though its direct audience is primarily players and experimenters.
impact_evidence: The game makes the human indispensable rather than treating them as an obstacle.
Co-op puzzle format provides an experiential way to understand agent collaboration.
Three-level scope gives a concrete playable use case.
creativity_rationale: Making the agent a constrained teammate and treating the missing tool as the central game design is genuinely original and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: The missing human-movement tool is explicitly the whole design, not a limitation by accident.
Levels are mathematically screened for the required interdependence.
Final level introduces reciprocal door/plate coordination.
usability_note: A no-build, dependency-free game with hints, reset, and level changes suggests strong accessibility for the intended demo audience.
red_flags: No submitted frame sheets or video, so visual polish and actual play cannot be assessed.
standouts: WebMCP capability boundaries are the core mechanic.
Formal solver validation supports intentional level design.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and creativity with concrete implementation evidence.

one_line: A browser anime-production studio where agents orchestrate writing, visuals, animation, voice, scoring, and editing.
what_it_does: Provides projects, shot pages, compose/generate consoles, comp editing, timeline, jobs, and backend settings so an agent can operate a complex film pipeline while the creator guides it.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP can make a large, difficult-to-navigate production surface discoverable and repeatable for agents, but the same pipeline appears operable through its existing UI with effort.
leverage_evidence: Description says the studio publishes its many toggles, drawers, and controls as page tools.
Agent is intended to find and operate controls the creator cannot easily remember.
Claimed application includes structured shot, compose, generate, timeline, and jobs surfaces.
execution_rationale: The packet documents a substantial product with a 293-second video, 12 gallery images, live demo, and public repo; the scope is ambitious and likely has unfinished edges due to breadth.
execution_evidence: Live demo, public repository, 12 gallery images, and 293-second product video are reported.
Claimed 97 shots, 567 takes, and four-minute animatic demonstrate a serious underlying pipeline.
Application surface includes projects, editor, shot page, comp editor, timeline, jobs, and settings.
impact_rationale: Independent animators and creators have a real need to manage complex generative production workflows; the studio could reduce navigation and coordination burden while preserving creative direction.
impact_evidence: The author describes a concrete production pipeline spanning image, motion, compositing, voice, scoring, and editing.
Browser studio centralizes future-film control and hosted model backends.
Collaboration model keeps the creator guiding vision.
creativity_rationale: Turning a sprawling anime pipeline into an agent-operable production studio is an ambitious and memorable synthesis, with depth evidenced by the prior real workflow.
creativity_evidence: Combines multiple media-generation and editorial stages in one browser studio.
Uses WebMCP as a solution to complexity and discoverability rather than merely adding a chat panel.
Four-minute animatic and hundreds of takes indicate sustained pursuit.
usability_note: The product explicitly grew into a Photoshop-sized surface that even its author found hard to navigate; agent discoverability helps but overall usability remains a risk.
red_flags: The underlying production pipeline and application predate the challenge, based on the narrative.
Very broad surface may have incomplete or confusing workflow edges.
standouts: WebMCP addresses surface complexity and discoverability directly.
advance_reason: Strong execution evidence and ambitious creative scope; WebMCP contribution is meaningful but not fully indispensable.

one_line: A safety simulator where agents investigate incidents while human approvals gate dangerous tools.
what_it_does: Lets an agent inspect evidence and propose mitigations, dynamically narrows tool schemas, logs decisions, and enables risky execution only after trusted approvals.
leverage_rationale: The product demonstrates WebMCP-native safety through conditional tool registration and live schema narrowing; general UI automation cannot reproduce these boundaries as cleanly or reliably.
leverage_evidence: Dangerous action tool is never registered until human approval.
Revoking a service live-narrows the WebMCP tool schema, not only the UI.
Blocked calls, approvals, and execute_approved_action are part of the shared workflow.
execution_rationale: The packet specifies a complete simulator workflow with visible state, blocked attempts, approvals, recovery, and scorecard, supported by a live demo, repo, and frame sheets; no video limits direct proof.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repository are reported alive.
Claimed scorecard checks root cause, mitigation, and prompt-injection resistance.
Description reports visible evidence, decision context, activity log, blocked banner, approvals, and service recovery.
impact_rationale: Production incidents and prompt injection are real high-stakes problems for teams adopting agents in operational systems; a safe simulator offers credible training and design value.
impact_evidence: Scenario models a checkout outage and production-changing mitigation.
Prompt-injection note is explicitly tested and not obeyed.
Human approval, written reasons, revocation, and auditability address operational risk.
creativity_rationale: The combination of incident response simulation, dynamic tool surface, prompt-injection scoring, and trusted multi-approval is a notably strong WebMCP interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Dangerous capability absence, rather than a disabled button, is used as the safety primitive.
Scorecard makes safety behavior an observable game-like evaluation.
Decision context and tool activity are designed for joint human-agent reasoning.
usability_note: The claimed unclipped activity log, explicit blocked banner, and visible decision context suggest a well-designed operator experience.
red_flags: No video/transcript; agent behavior and recovery are described but not directly shown in motion.
standouts: Schema-level gating and live narrowing are stronger than UI-only safety theater.
Prompt-injection resistance is tested as part of the scorecard.
advance_reason: One of the strongest packets: high WebMCP indispensability, real operational relevance, and a coherent safety workflow.

one_line: A WebMCP consent layer that lets agents explain policies while humans make the final choice.
what_it_does: Exposes consent decisions and policy clauses for agent inspection, consequence analysis, and plain-language explanation before human approval.
leverage_rationale: Structured access to consent state and relevant clauses can improve agent precision and shared context, but policy summarization and consent UI are also achievable through ordinary browser automation.
leverage_evidence: Description says the agent can inspect decisions, consequences, relevant clauses, and explain them.
Human remains the final decision-maker rather than giving the agent an accept button.
Frame sheets are submitted, but the packet text is heavily malformed and no video exists.
execution_rationale: The concept is coherent, but the packet provides thin and malformed evidence, no repo, and no video; completeness of the actual consent workflow is unclear.
execution_evidence: Live demo and four gallery images are reported.
About text consistently states a consent-understanding workflow.
No public repository, video, or transcript; extracted text contains substantial formatting loss and truncation.
impact_rationale: People routinely accept opaque terms and cookie policies, and informed consent is a clear audience need; the proposed human-in-the-loop explanation addresses that need.
impact_evidence: Description identifies habitual blind acceptance of terms and cookie tracking.
Agent is tasked with finding relevant clauses and explaining consequences in plain language.
Human final decision is explicitly preserved.
creativity_rationale: The consent-explanation use case is valuable but familiar; the WebMCP-specific human-final-decision framing adds a real angle without being radically novel.
creativity_evidence: Applies agent tools to consent comprehension rather than automatic acceptance.
Connects policy clause retrieval, consequence explanation, and final human choice.
usability_note: The intended interaction is understandable, but the supplied evidence is too degraded to assess the interface or flow quality.
red_flags: Malformed/truncated About text and no video or public repo make execution difficult to verify.
No readable evidence of an actual completed consent decision.
standouts: Keeps agency with the human at the precise point of consent.
advance_reason: Good problem and plausible concept, but evidence is too thin to support advancement against stronger packets.

one_line: A consent-driven bridge that resumes agent tasks when later business events occur.
what_it_does: Connects future host events to an existing agent task, with event permissions, preserved strategy context, and revocation; demonstrated through a persistent game host.
leverage_rationale: Continuity beyond a browser session and event-triggered resumption are capabilities ordinary page-driving agents cannot provide reliably without a dedicated bridge and shared state.
leverage_evidence: Core pitch is continuity beyond a browser session and bringing agents back on real events.
User approves which events may resume a task and can revoke permission.
Original strategy conversation is preserved while live page state grounds continuation.
execution_rationale: The concept and host demo are coherent, but there is no public repo or video and the packet does not show the trigger/resume sequence end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Live demo and five frame sheets are reported.
Description gives a specific Host application, Sleepless Kingdom, and a persistent-world waiting scenario.
Claimed architecture includes event permissions, continuation, and revocation.
impact_rationale: Many useful agent workflows pause for external review or asynchronous events; removing the user as message relay has clear productivity value while retaining consent.
impact_evidence: Job applications and other workflows are described as stopping while awaiting another party.
Event-based return reduces the need to find the conversation and manually resume it.
Permission and revocation address user-control concerns.
creativity_rationale: Event-driven re-entry for an existing agent conversation is a genuinely novel WebMCP-adjacent interaction model, and the persistent-game framing makes the waiting problem memorable.
creativity_evidence: Treats asynchronous continuation as a first-class web capability rather than another notification.
Uses a persistent game world to make temporal continuity legible.
Consent-driven event selection and revocation add depth beyond simple webhooks.
usability_note: The permission model sounds understandable, but the actual resume experience is not directly demonstrated in the packet text.
red_flags: No public repo or video/transcript; core asynchronous trigger is claimed rather than proven.
Cloud bridge and event delivery details are not evidenced.
standouts: Strongest continuity/async concept in the packet.
Human consent and revocation are integrated into re-entry.
advance_reason: Transformative continuity concept with clear impact and high creativity; execution evidence needs Stage 2 verification.

one_line: A governed creative workbench that routes evidence through review and provenance-preserving export.
what_it_does: Moves a creator’s premise through Spark, Sources, Locks, Quampute, Review, and Export while separating confirmed and derived conclusions and gating paid or consequential actions.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP supports explicit tool inputs, side effects, boundaries, provenance, and continuity across a complex creative workflow; a general agent driving UI would be less reliable and auditable.
leverage_evidence: Six visible stages are described with structured evidence routing and review state.
Creator-owned truths, identity, consent, locks, cost, deletion, and publication remain gated.
Export explicitly preserves provenance and does not falsely claim compilation or runtime testing.
execution_rationale: The packet is unusually explicit about scope, deterministic example content, QA states, and honest export boundaries, with live demo and public repo; no video and zero gallery images reduce direct evidence.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repository are reported alive.
Deterministic no-cost museum-registrar example uses synthetic 29-tab, 607-question source material.
Workflow states and export limitations are clearly enumerated.
impact_rationale: Creators and knowledge workers need dependable evidence handling and provenance when using agents for complex work; the product addresses hallucination, consent, and consequential-action risks directly.
impact_evidence: Description identifies the failure of chat-box creative tools to preserve identity, taste, boundaries, and evidence.
Review distinguishes confirmed, derived, adapted, reserved, and not-applicable conclusions.
Honest export avoids false claims about compilation, installation, testing, or publication.
creativity_rationale: The evidence-routed ‘Quampute’ workflow and explicit separation of creator identity from agent synthesis are a distinctive interaction model with meaningful depth.
creativity_evidence: Six-stage creative workflow is more structured than a generic generation chat.
Provenance and creator-owned locks are treated as product primitives.
Agent is assigned reading, routing, checking, deriving, and preserving rather than ownership of consequential decisions.
usability_note: The governance model is thoughtful but the many stages and classifications may impose cognitive load; no visual gallery evidence was supplied.
red_flags: No gallery images or video/transcript; most execution claims are textual.
Very broad creative-workbench scope may hide unfinished paths.
standouts: Creator/agent role differentiation is unusually explicit.
advance_reason: High-quality governance concept with substantial structured workflow and strong evidence honesty, warranting further verification.

one_line: A mutual-prediction game where humans and AI agents compete and cooperate over image associations.
what_it_does: Both parties choose words connected to an image while predicting and blocking the other’s choices; solo and team modes make the agent a participant rather than a hidden engine.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP enables the agent to participate as an explicit game player with a separate channel and shared round state; generic UI automation could imitate this but less cleanly and with less intentional separation.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly says the agent is playing the game, not powering the interface.
Solo mode pits human against agent; team mode pairs each with an agent.
Mutual prediction and blocking require shared turn/round state.
execution_rationale: The concept is clear and has a live demo, public repo, three frame sheets, and gallery images, but no video and limited packet detail about scoring, state handling, or completeness.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repository are reported alive.
Description specifies solo, team, and coordination phases.
Three gallery images and frame sheets provide packaging/product evidence, though no transcript exists.
impact_rationale: It has credible entertainment value and can help people learn how human and agent perception differ, though the broader educational impact is aspirational.
impact_evidence: Game is designed around complementary human intuition and agent strengths.
Description positions it as an easy way to observe and learn to work with agents.
Team mode creates a concrete social collaboration experience.
creativity_rationale: Making perception and unpredictability—not speed or logic—the basis for a human-agent game is an original design choice pursued across competitive and cooperative modes.
creativity_evidence: Explicitly avoids logic and reaction games to balance human and agent strengths.
Prediction/blocking mechanic makes the difference in perception playable.
Human-plus-agent teams compete against another human-plus-agent team.
usability_note: Simple word-choice rounds should be approachable, though frame evidence is insufficient to assess onboarding and interaction polish.
red_flags: No video/transcript and limited detail on actual agent invocation.
WebMCP delta may be reproducible with other structured agent APIs, despite being central to the game.
standouts: Agent is a player with its own strengths, not a concealed assistant.
Thoughtful balancing around intuition and perception.
advance_reason: Memorable, category-appropriate game concept with meaningful agent participation and credible demo evidence.

one_line: A human-governed WebMCP boundary where agents ask for capabilities and receive answers without taking datasets.
what_it_does: Lets agents propose data sources and ask questions; page owners approve capabilities, tools can appear after approval, and responses are returned without exposing the underlying rows.
leverage_rationale: The product makes human approval, dynamic tool creation, answer-only data access, and per-source direct/ask-only policy part of the page’s live agent surface—capabilities not reliably reproduced by generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Agent may call ask_data_source/propose_data_source but cannot fetch or create without owner approval.
A tool that did not exist becomes available after approval in the same conversation.
Claimed answer returned while 28 dataset rows remain on page, with receipt and backend verification.
Same registry is published as an A2A Agent Card for agents outside the browser.
execution_rationale: The packet gives concrete rejected/approved paths, dynamic registry behavior, receipts, backend verification, a live demo, public repo, and extensive gallery evidence; no video still limits direct observation.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repository are reported alive with 13 gallery images.
Acceptance script reportedly asserts the boundary against the live deployment.
Description distinguishes rejected no-backend-action, approved creation, answer-only response, and direct mode.
impact_rationale: Websites with valuable data need a practical way to answer agents while controlling capability grants and protecting datasets; the owner-centric model addresses a real emerging governance problem.
impact_evidence: Description targets ordinary websites that have useful information but no safe agent interaction boundary.
Answer-only semantics protect source rows while still enabling useful computation.
Per-source owner decisions and no-cost rejected proposals provide concrete control.
creativity_rationale: Dynamic, human-approved capability creation combined with dataset non-disclosure and dual WebMCP/A2A exposure is an unusually ambitious and memorable protocol design.
creativity_evidence: Ask-only by default is contrasted with direct access per source.
Capability can be created after approval during the same conversation.
Receipt records what was consulted and what remained private.
usability_note: The visible approval/rejection and receipt model should make boundaries legible, though actual agent UX is not shown in a video.
red_flags: No submitted video/transcript; several strongest claims rely on acceptance-script description rather than visible motion.
A2A exposure broadens scope beyond WebMCP and should not be over-credited for WebMCP leverage.
standouts: Answer-not-dataset boundary is concrete and testable.
Dynamic tools after human approval are a strong shared-state demonstration.
advance_reason: Excellent WebMCP leverage and creativity with concrete security boundaries, dynamic capability approval, and strong claimed validation.
